SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT
SELLER COUNTERPROPOSAL — SUBJECT TO CONTRACT AND SELLER APPROVAL
This draft is for negotiation only and does not create a binding obligation. Bracketed matters and referenced schedules require agreement before execution.

1. Purchase Price and Completion Accounts.
1.1 The Seller proposes an enterprise value of USD 42,000,000 for the business on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. The equity purchase price for all issued Shares shall equal that amount, plus unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, less financial indebtedness, agreed debt-like items and unpaid Company transaction expenses, and plus or minus the amount by which Closing working capital exceeds or falls below an agreed normalized working-capital target. Definitions, the target, illustrative calculations and an exhaustive schedule of agreed debt-like items shall be agreed before signing. No item shall be counted more than once, including under the price adjustment, leakage or indemnity provisions.
1.2 At least five Business Days before Closing, the Seller shall provide a good-faith estimated completion statement with supporting calculations. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the estimated equity purchase price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Seller's designated account, less the escrow deposit under clause 3.4, which shall be paid to the escrow agent on the Seller's behalf.
1.3 Within 60 days after Closing, the Buyer shall deliver completion accounts and its proposed final equity purchase price. The Seller shall have 30 days to review and give a reasonably detailed dispute notice; undisputed items shall become final. The parties shall provide reasonable access to relevant records and personnel. Unresolved accounting disputes after 20 Business Days of good-faith discussion shall be referred to an independent accountant jointly appointed, or appointed through an agreed independent appointing body if the parties cannot agree. The accountant shall act as expert, not arbitrator, determine only disputed items within the parties' submitted positions, and apply the agreed accounting policies; its determination shall be binding absent manifest error or fraud. Its costs shall be allocated by reference to relative success. Completion accounts shall follow the specific policies agreed at signing, then the consistently applied policies of the reference accounts, and then the agreed accounting framework; no purchase accounting or changes arising from Buyer's post-Closing decisions shall be included. Any balancing payment shall be made within five Business Days after final determination.
1.4 No party may withhold or set off a disputed claim against consideration or another payment. Set-off shall be permitted only for amounts admitted in writing by the payee or finally determined by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, subject to the agreed liability limits, escrow-first recovery provisions and prohibition on double recovery.

2. Closing, Conditions and Termination.
2.1 The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing. Closing shall occur within five Business Days after satisfaction or lawful waiver of the agreed conditions, other than conditions to be satisfied at Closing. The proposed outside date is 60 days after signing, extendable by written agreement.
2.2 Buyer's satisfactory diligence shall be completed before execution of the definitive agreement. Any diligence matter remaining at signing must be identified expressly and converted into an objective, time-limited condition or other agreed protection; there shall be no general post-signing discretionary diligence condition.
2.3 Closing conditions shall include receipt of specifically scheduled mandatory regulatory approvals and material third-party consents; absence of a legal prohibition; accuracy of fundamental representations in all material respects and other representations except for inaccuracies that, taken together, have a material adverse effect, avoiding duplicative materiality qualifications; performance in all material respects of pre-Closing covenants; absence of a defined material adverse change; and delivery of the agreed Closing documents. Conditions benefiting a party may be waived by that party only where lawful. The approval and consent schedule remains subject to verification and agreement.
2.4 Material adverse change shall mean a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition or results of the Company, excluding general economic, market, industry and legal changes except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company relative to comparable businesses. Failure to meet forecasts alone shall not constitute such a change, without excluding independently qualifying underlying causes.
2.5 Each party shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain required approvals and consents and satisfy its conditions. Neither party shall be required to accept a material divestiture or other material remedy unless specifically agreed. There shall be no financing condition.
2.6 Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by the outside date or a final, nonappealable legal prohibition prevents Closing, but not if its own material breach caused the failure to close. A nonbreaching party may terminate for the other's material breach that prevents satisfaction of a Closing condition and remains uncured for 15 Business Days after notice, or is incapable of cure. Termination shall preserve accrued rights for prior breach and the confidentiality, costs and dispute-resolution provisions.
2.7 Seller's Closing deliverables shall include duly executed share transfers, share certificates or agreed substitutes, evidence of authority, scheduled approvals and consents, agreed resignations, releases of relevant security interests, Company registers and records, and a conditions certificate. Buyer shall deliver payment, evidence of authority, its conditions certificate and executed escrow documents. The detailed deliverables and mechanics shall be scheduled before signing.

3. Representations, Covenants and Liability.
3.1 The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller representations concerning title to the Shares free of encumbrances, authority and enforceability, capitalization, financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, tax, material contracts, litigation, legal compliance, employment, intellectual property and material assets. Financial statements shall fairly present the Company's financial position and results in all material respects under the agreed accounting framework, with agreed qualifications for interim accounts. Business representations shall have appropriate materiality and defined actual-knowledge qualifications following reasonable inquiry of named personnel. Representations shall be qualified by a disclosure schedule fairly identifying the nature and scope of disclosed matters; any general data-room disclosure must be expressly agreed. Buyer shall represent its authority, enforceability and availability of funds at Closing. The complete representation language and disclosure schedule must be agreed before signing.
3.2 From signing to Closing, the Seller shall procure that the Company operates in the ordinary course and preserves its business in all material respects. Without Buyer's consent, not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, the Company shall not make distributions, issue securities, incur material nonordinary-course debt, dispose of material assets, enter into or amend material nonordinary-course contracts, or materially increase compensation outside ordinary-course or existing contractual requirements. Exceptions shall cover agreed budgets, disclosed commitments, legal requirements and reasonably necessary emergency measures with prompt notice. Buyer shall have reasonable information access without operational control before Closing.
3.3 No transfer of value to the Seller or its connected persons outside agreed permitted payments shall occur between signing and Closing. Any prohibited leakage shall be reimbursed dollar for dollar, but not to the extent already reflected in the purchase price or otherwise recovered.
3.4 Seller proposes an escrow equal to 5% of the final equity purchase price, initially funded at 5% of the estimated price and adjusted upon final determination, held by an independent agent for 18 months. General representation claims shall survive for 18 months and be subject to a USD 50,000 per-claim threshold, a deductible aggregate basket of 1% of the final equity purchase price and an aggregate cap of 10%. Fundamental representations shall survive six years and be capped at the final equity purchase price. Tax claims shall survive until 60 days after the applicable statutory assessment period, subject to that same cap. Covenant claims shall survive for the applicable contractual performance period plus 12 months. Timely notified claims describing their basis and estimated amount shall survive until resolved. Escrow releases shall require joint instructions or a final binding determination; at expiry, funds shall be released except for reasonably reserved amounts for timely notified unresolved claims. Buyer shall seek recovery from escrow first where available; escrow is security, not an increase in liability limits.
3.5 Seller shall indemnify Buyer for proven loss from breaches of Seller's representations and covenants, subject to the agreed limitations. A tax covenant shall cover pre-Closing taxes, with agreed allocation of straddle-period taxes and conduct of tax disputes, excluding taxes already reflected in the price and taxes caused by Buyer's post-Closing actions outside the ordinary course unless legally required. Claim procedures shall require reasonable notice, mitigation, appropriate defense participation and consent to settlements imposing liability or admissions on another party. Recovery shall be reduced by actual insurance recoveries and realized tax benefits, net of associated costs. No double recovery or punitive damages shall be recoverable, except punitive damages payable to a third party. Fundamental, tax and leakage claims shall not be subject to the general basket or threshold. Seller's aggregate contractual liability shall not exceed the final equity purchase price. No limitation shall exclude liability for the liable party's fraud or liability that cannot lawfully be limited. The definitive agreement shall specify exclusive contractual remedies while preserving expressly agreed equitable relief.

4. Confidentiality and General Provisions.
4.1 Each party shall keep confidential transaction information, the terms of this proposed Agreement and the negotiations, except information lawfully public or independently obtained without breach. Disclosure may be made as required by law, with advance notice where lawful, or on a need-to-know basis to professional advisers, affiliates and bona fide prospective financing sources and their advisers who are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties providing substantially equivalent protection. The disclosing party shall be responsible for breaches by its permitted recipients. Sensitive information shall remain subject to agreed data-room, clean-team and personal-data safeguards. No public announcement may be made without the other's prior written consent except as legally required. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains effective pending an express agreement on its relationship with the definitive agreement.
4.2 Each party shall bear its own transaction costs. Any Company transaction expenses paid through the price adjustment shall not also be charged to the Seller separately. Allocation of transfer taxes shall be agreed before signing.
4.3 Notices shall be in writing to the addresses and designated email contacts specified in the definitive agreement. Deemed receipt rules, including treatment of non-Business Days and failed electronic delivery, shall be agreed before signing.
4.4 Governing law and the exclusive court or arbitral forum shall be agreed before signing. Accounting disputes under clause 1.3 shall remain subject to expert determination. The definitive agreement shall include entire-agreement, amendment, assignment, counterparts and severability provisions.

SHARE PURCHASE AGREEMENT — NONBINDING DISCUSSION DRAFT
Subject to contract and Seller approval. This draft records proposed terms only and creates no obligation to sell, buy or consummate the transaction unless and until definitive documentation is executed. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains unaffected.

1. Purchase Price and Payment. The Seller proposes a base purchase price of USD 45,000,000 for the Shares on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital. The Buyer’s USD 35,000,000 counterproposal has not been accepted. The definitive agreement shall specify the treatment of cash, indebtedness, debt-like items and transaction expenses, an agreed normalized working-capital target and accounting policies, and completion-account adjustments without double counting. An estimated Closing payment shall be reconciled against completion accounts through agreed preparation and objection deadlines, mutual access to supporting records and determination of unresolved accounting items by an independent accountant acting as expert. Payment shall be by wire transfer of immediately available funds, subject only to any expressly agreed escrow and legally required withholding. Seller account instructions shall be authenticated before payment; initial instructions and any subsequent changes must be independently verified through a previously established contact using independently verified contact details, and not solely by reply to the communication providing the instructions.

2. Diligence, Closing Conditions and Interim Conduct. The Buyer shall complete its financial, tax, legal and commercial diligence before signing definitive documentation; there shall be no post-signing subjective diligence or financing condition. Closing shall occur promptly following satisfaction or lawful waiver by the party entitled to its benefit of the agreed conditions, with a target of 30 days after signing. The Seller proposes an outside date of 60 days after signing, subject to an expressly agreed extension mechanism for outstanding regulatory approvals. Conditions shall include required regulatory and identified material third-party approvals; release at Closing of encumbrances over the Shares; delivery of customary share-transfer documents, corporate authorizations and payment; accuracy of fundamental warranties in all material respects and of other warranties subject to an agreed material-adverse-effect standard, with appropriate treatment of existing materiality qualifications and date-specific warranties; material compliance with interim covenants; and absence of a material adverse change under an agreed definition. That definition shall exclude general economic, market and industry changes, changes in law or accounting standards and effects of the announcement of the transaction, with a negotiated disproportionate-impact exception where appropriate. The parties shall use agreed reasonable efforts to secure approvals and satisfy conditions. Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by the outside date, unless its own material breach caused the failure to close; the definitive agreement shall also provide termination rights for a final legal prohibition and an uncured material breach preventing satisfaction of a Closing condition, with appropriate notice and cure periods. Termination shall preserve accrued rights for prior breach and expressly surviving obligations.
Between signing and Closing, the Seller shall procure operation of the business in the ordinary course in all material respects. Except as disclosed and agreed, required by law or expressly contemplated by the definitive agreement, distributions, new indebtedness outside agreed ordinary-course limits and material transactions outside the ordinary course shall require Buyer consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. The Buyer shall receive reasonable information access on notice, subject to confidentiality, privilege, applicable law and noninterference with the business; access shall not confer pre-Closing operational control.

3. Warranties, Disclosure and Claims. The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller warranties addressing authority and enforceability; ownership of and title to the Shares; capitalization; financial statements and undisclosed liabilities; taxes; material contracts; litigation; legal compliance; employment; intellectual property; and insolvency. Business warranties shall be subject to appropriate, specifically negotiated knowledge and materiality qualifications and matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail in disclosure schedules delivered and agreed before signing. Post-signing disclosures shall not automatically cure a breach or qualify a Closing condition without the Buyer’s agreement. The Seller shall coordinate preparation of the disclosure schedules alongside pre-signing diligence, subject to privilege, confidentiality and applicable law.
The definitive agreement shall provide contractual remedies for warranty breaches, a negotiated pre-Closing tax indemnity and any specifically agreed diligence-related indemnities. The Seller proposes an 18-month survival period for general business warranties, a general warranty liability cap of 10% of the final purchase price and an aggregate deductible basket of 1%, with a per-claim de minimis threshold to be agreed. Fundamental warranty claims shall be subject to a separate cap not exceeding the final purchase price and an agreed longer survival period; tax claims shall have separately agreed limitations and survival tied to the applicable statutory period. Any fraud exception shall be carefully defined and shall not limit liability that cannot lawfully be limited. The Seller proposes an escrow of 5% of the Closing purchase price for 18 months, credited against and not additional to applicable liability caps, with release of the balance at expiry except for reasonably quantified amounts relating to properly notified outstanding claims. No additional holdback is proposed. Claims provisions shall address notice, defense and settlement of third-party claims, mitigation, recoveries under insurance or from third parties, and prevention of double recovery. Contractual remedies shall be exclusive to the extent permitted by law, subject to agreed fraud and equitable-relief exceptions. These limitations, escrow terms and survival periods remain proposals for negotiation, not agreed terms.

4. Confidentiality and Announcements. The definitive agreement shall require each party to keep confidential the transaction terms, negotiations and nonpublic information received in connection with the transaction, subject to customary exclusions for information lawfully public or independently obtained without breach of duty. Disclosure shall be permitted on a need-to-know basis to professional advisers and, for the Buyer, its affiliates, prospective financing sources and their advisers, provided recipients are bound by professional duties or contractual confidentiality obligations appropriate to the information and no less protective in substance. Each disclosing party shall be responsible for breaches by its permitted recipients, subject to any expressly agreed exception for recipients directly bound to the other party. Disclosure may also be made with the other party’s prior written consent or to the extent required by applicable law, regulation or legal process. Where legally permitted, the disclosing party shall give prompt prior notice, cooperate reasonably in seeking confidential treatment and disclose only what is required. Public announcements shall require prior agreement on timing and content, except where legally required, in which case the announcing party shall consult the other party in advance where legally permitted. Existing binding confidentiality obligations remain in force pending execution of definitive documentation.

1.2 At least five Business Days before Closing, the Seller shall provide a good-faith estimated completion statement with supporting calculations. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the estimated equity purchase price by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the Seller's designated account, less the escrow deposit under clause 3.4, which shall be paid to the escrow agent on the Seller's behalf.
1.3 Within 60 days after Closing, the Buyer shall deliver completion accounts and its proposed final equity purchase price. The Seller shall have 30 days to review and give a reasonably detailed dispute notice; undisputed items shall become final. The parties shall provide reasonable access to relevant records and personnel. Unresolved accounting disputes after 20 Business Days of good-faith discussion shall be referred to an independent accountant jointly appointed, or appointed through an agreed independent appointing body if the parties cannot agree. The accountant shall act as expert, not arbitrator, determine only disputed items within the parties' submitted positions, and apply the agreed accounting policies; its determination shall be binding absent manifest error or fraud. Its costs shall be allocated by reference to relative success. Completion accounts shall follow the specific policies agreed at signing, then the consistently applied policies of the reference accounts, and then the agreed accounting framework; no purchase accounting or changes arising from Buyer's post-Closing decisions shall be included. Any balancing payment shall be made within five Business Days after final determination.
1.4 No party may withhold or set off a disputed claim against consideration or another payment. Set-off shall be permitted only for amounts admitted in writing by the payee or finally determined by a court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, subject to the agreed liability limits, escrow-first recovery provisions and prohibition on double recovery.
  [2] 2. Closing, Conditions and Termination.
2.1 The parties shall target Closing within 30 days after signing. Closing shall occur within five Business Days after satisfaction or lawful waiver of the agreed conditions, other than conditions to be satisfied at Closing. The proposed outside date is 60 days after signing, extendable by written agreement.
2.2 Buyer's satisfactory diligence shall be completed before execution of the definitive agreement. Any diligence matter remaining at signing must be identified expressly and converted into an objective, time-limited condition or other agreed protection; there shall be no general post-signing discretionary diligence condition.
2.3 Closing conditions shall include receipt of specifically scheduled mandatory regulatory approvals and material third-party consents; absence of a legal prohibition; accuracy of fundamental representations in all material respects and other representations except for inaccuracies that, taken together, have a material adverse effect, avoiding duplicative materiality qualifications; performance in all material respects of pre-Closing covenants; absence of a defined material adverse change; and delivery of the agreed Closing documents. Conditions benefiting a party may be waived by that party only where lawful. The approval and consent schedule remains subject to verification and agreement.
2.4 Material adverse change shall mean a material adverse effect on the business, financial condition or results of the Company, excluding general economic, market, industry and legal changes except to the extent disproportionately affecting the Company relative to comparable businesses. Failure to meet forecasts alone shall not constitute such a change, without excluding independently qualifying underlying causes.
2.5 Each party shall use reasonable best efforts to obtain required approvals and consents and satisfy its conditions. Neither party shall be required to accept a material divestiture or other material remedy unless specifically agreed. There shall be no financing condition.
2.6 Either party may terminate if Closing has not occurred by the outside date or a final, nonappealable legal prohibition prevents Closing, but not if its own material breach caused the failure to close. A nonbreaching party may terminate for the other's material breach that prevents satisfaction of a Closing condition and remains uncured for 15 Business Days after notice, or is incapable of cure. Termination shall preserve accrued rights for prior breach and the confidentiality, costs and dispute-resolution provisions.
2.7 Seller's Closing deliverables shall include duly executed share transfers, share certificates or agreed substitutes, evidence of authority, scheduled approvals and consents, agreed resignations, releases of relevant security interests, Company registers and records, and a conditions certificate. Buyer shall deliver payment, evidence of authority, its conditions certificate and executed escrow documents. The detailed deliverables and mechanics shall be scheduled before signing.
  [3] 3. Representations, Covenants and Liability.
3.1 The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller representations concerning title to the Shares free of encumbrances, authority and enforceability, capitalization, financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, tax, material contracts, litigation, legal compliance, employment, intellectual property and material assets. Financial statements shall fairly present the Company's financial position and results in all material respects under the agreed accounting framework, with agreed qualifications for interim accounts. Business representations shall have appropriate materiality and defined actual-knowledge qualifications following reasonable inquiry of named personnel. Representations shall be qualified by a disclosure schedule fairly identifying the nature and scope of disclosed matters; any general data-room disclosure must be expressly agreed. Buyer shall represent its authority, enforceability and availability of funds at Closing. The complete representation language and disclosure schedule must be agreed before signing.
3.2 From signing to Closing, the Seller shall procure that the Company operates in the ordinary course and preserves its business in all material respects. Without Buyer's consent, not unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, the Company shall not make distributions, issue securities, incur material nonordinary-course debt, dispose of material assets, enter into or amend material nonordinary-course contracts, or materially increase compensation outside ordinary-course or existing contractual requirements. Exceptions shall cover agreed budgets, disclosed commitments, legal requirements and reasonably necessary emergency measures with prompt notice. Buyer shall have reasonable information access without operational control before Closing.
3.3 No transfer of value to the Seller or its connected persons outside agreed permitted payments shall occur between signing and Closing. Any prohibited leakage shall be reimbursed dollar for dollar, but not to the extent already reflected in the purchase price or otherwise recovered.
3.4 Seller proposes an escrow equal to 5% of the final equity purchase price, initially funded at 5% of the estimated price and adjusted upon final determination, held by an independent agent for 18 months. General representation claims shall survive for 18 months and be subject to a USD 50,000 per-claim threshold, a deductible aggregate basket of 1% of the final equity purchase price and an aggregate cap of 10%. Fundamental representations shall survive six years and be capped at the final equity purchase price. Tax claims shall survive until 60 days after the applicable statutory assessment period, subject to that same cap. Covenant claims shall survive for the applicable contractual performance period plus 12 months. Timely notified claims describing their basis and estimated amount shall survive until resolved. Escrow releases shall require joint instructions or a final binding determination; at expiry, funds shall be released except for reasonably reserved amounts for timely notified unresolved claims. Buyer shall seek recovery from escrow first where available; escrow is security, not an increase in liability limits.
3.5 Seller shall indemnify Buyer for proven loss from breaches of Seller's representations and covenants, subject to the agreed limitations. A tax covenant shall cover pre-Closing taxes, with agreed allocation of straddle-period taxes and conduct of tax disputes, excluding taxes already reflected in the price and taxes caused by Buyer's post-Closing actions outside the ordinary course unless legally required. Claim procedures shall require reasonable notice, mitigation, appropriate defense participation and consent to settlements imposing liability or admissions on another party. Recovery shall be reduced by actual insurance recoveries and realized tax benefits, net of associated costs. No double recovery or punitive damages shall be recoverable, except punitive damages payable to a third party. Fundamental, tax and leakage claims shall not be subject to the general basket or threshold. Seller's aggregate contractual liability shall not exceed the final equity purchase price. No limitation shall exclude liability for the liable party's fraud or liability that cannot lawfully be limited. The definitive agreement shall specify exclusive contractual remedies while preserving expressly agreed equitable relief.
  [4] 4. Confidentiality and General Provisions.
4.1 Each party shall keep confidential transaction information, the terms of this proposed Agreement and the negotiations, except information lawfully public or independently obtained without breach. Disclosure may be made as required by law, with advance notice where lawful, or on a need-to-know basis to professional advisers, affiliates and bona fide prospective financing sources and their advisers who are bound by confidentiality obligations or professional duties providing substantially equivalent protection. The disclosing party shall be responsible for breaches by its permitted recipients. Sensitive information shall remain subject to agreed data-room, clean-team and personal-data safeguards. No public announcement may be made without the other's prior written consent except as legally required. Any existing confidentiality agreement remains effective pending an express agreement on its relationship with the definitive agreement.
4.2 Each party shall bear its own transaction costs. Any Company transaction expenses paid through the price adjustment shall not also be charged to the Seller separately. Allocation of transfer taxes shall be agreed before signing.
4.3 Notices shall be in writing to the addresses and designated email contacts specified in the definitive agreement. Deemed receipt rules, including treatment of non-Business Days and failed electronic delivery, shall be agreed before signing.
4.4 Governing law and the exclusive court or arbitral forum shall be agreed before signing. Accounting disputes under clause 1.3 shall remain subject to expert determination. The definitive agreement shall include entire-agreement, amendment, assignment, counterparts and severability provisions.

The definitive agreement shall contain negotiated Seller warranties addressing authority and enforceability; ownership of and title to the Shares; capitalization; financial statements and undisclosed liabilities; taxes; material contracts; litigation; legal compliance; employment; intellectual property; and insolvency. Post-signing disclosures shall not automatically cure a breach or qualify a Closing condition without the Buyer’s agreement. The Seller shall coordinate preparation of the disclosure schedules alongside pre-signing diligence, subject to privilege, confidentiality and applicable law.

Contractual remedies shall be exclusive to the extent permitted by law, subject to agreed fraud and equitable-relief exceptions. These limitations, escrow terms and survival periods remain proposals for negotiation, not agreed terms.

The definitive agreement shall require each party to keep confidential the transaction terms, negotiations and nonpublic information received in connection with the transaction, subject to customary exclusions for information lawfully public or independently obtained without breach of duty. 1. Price: Replace the proposed USD 45,000,000 base price with Buyer’s USD 35,000,000 proposal, subject to satisfactory pre-signing diligence, agreed adjustments and definitive documentation. Specify the equity-price bridge and prohibit double counting across cash, debt, debt-like items, transaction expenses and working capital.

2. Working capital and completion accounts: Set the target using average monthly normalized operating working capital over the latest 12 completed months, tested against a 24-month history for seasonality and recent trading. Define included accounts and normalizations in an agreed illustrative schedule. Exclude cash, financing debt, income-tax balances and Seller transaction expenses to the extent separately accounted for. Address aged receivables, inventory obsolescence, accruals and deferred revenue expressly. Apply agreed transaction-specific policies first, then consistent historical policies to the extent compliant with the agreed accounting framework. Provide a dollar-for-dollar adjustment, an estimated statement five business days before Closing, Buyer’s completion accounts within 90 days after Closing and Seller’s objections within 30 days after receipt. Allow 20 business days to resolve objections before referring only disputed accounting items to an independent accountant; legal interpretation disputes remain for the agreed dispute forum. Provide reciprocal records access and prompt payment after final determination.

3. Prioritized diligence: First priority is three years of annual financial statements, 24 months of monthly management accounts and working-capital schedules, current year-to-date trading and budget comparisons, quality-of-earnings information, cash and debt schedules, receivables/payables aging, inventory reserves, transaction expenses and contingent or off-balance-sheet liabilities. In parallel, request capitalization and title records, shareholder arrangements, liens, material customer and supplier contracts, change-of-control consents, regulatory approvals, tax returns and audits, litigation and compliance matters. Next request employment and benefit arrangements, IP ownership and licensing, cybersecurity/privacy matters, insurance, property and environmental information where relevant, and draft disclosure schedules. Privileged or restricted materials should be identified by category and addressed through lawful alternatives, redaction or clean-team arrangements, without requiring privilege waiver.

4. Closing: Accept the 30-day target and 60-day outside date in principle, with an agreed regulatory extension. No post-signing subjective diligence condition is needed if diligence and schedules are completed before signing. Any commitment without a financing condition requires Buyer approval and funding readiness before signing. Fundamental warranties should be accurate in all respects, save immaterial inaccuracies where appropriate; other warranties should be brought down in all material respects without duplicative materiality qualifiers, rather than only to a material-adverse-effect threshold. Require releases of agreed business liens and debt payoff documentation as well as clean title to the Shares.

5. Interim protections: Prohibit distributions, value leakage, related-party transfers and extraordinary indebtedness without express Buyer consent. Apply a reasonable-consent standard to appropriate ordinary commercial matters, not automatic permission for leakage. Preserve lawful pre-Closing operational independence.

6. Remedies: Buyer proposes 24-month general warranty survival, a 20% general cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and no separate de minimis pending review of claim exposure. Fundamental warranties should have a purchase-price cap and six-year survival, subject to applicable law; tax survival should extend 60 days beyond the relevant statutory assessment period, including extensions. Tax and specific indemnities should sit outside the general warranty basket and cap, with their own agreed limits. Seek a 10% escrow for 24 months, preserving reasonably quantified pending claims and direct recourse against Seller for liabilities exceeding escrow. Escrow is security, not a separate liability cap. Preserve legally available fraud remedies and appropriate equitable relief. Timely notified claims must survive until resolved, and delayed notice should bar recovery only to the extent of material prejudice.

7. Documentation: Add governing law, dispute forum, notices and customary definitive-agreement provisions. Retain authenticated payment instructions, agreed pre-signing disclosure schedules and the rule against unilateral post-signing cure. All proposals remain nonbinding pending Buyer approval and execution.

Buyer’s proposal remains subject to diligence, agreed risk allocation, Buyer approval and definitive documentation.

Our immediate diligence priorities are: (i) three years of annual financials and 24 months of monthly accounts, current trading and budget comparisons; (ii) monthly working-capital detail, receivables/payables aging and inventory reserves; (iii) cash, indebtedness, debt-like liabilities and transaction expenses; (iv) capitalization, share title and liens; and (v) material contracts and consents, tax exposures, litigation and regulatory matters. Controlled disclosure and lawful privilege protections are acceptable; please identify restrictions so alternatives can be arranged.

Adjustments should be dollar-for-dollar and avoid duplication with debt, cash or expenses. Buyer would prepare completion accounts within 90 days, Seller would have 30 days to object, and unresolved accounting items would go to an independent accountant after a short resolution period.

We can work toward the proposed closing timetable, with a regulatory extension mechanism. Diligence and disclosure schedules must be completed before signing; acceptance of no financing condition remains subject to Buyer approval and funding readiness. We require a stronger warranty bring-down than the proposed MAE threshold and appropriate payoff and lien-release deliveries.

On remedies, our counterproposal is 24-month general survival, a 20% general cap, a 0.5% tipping basket and 10% escrow for 24 months. Fundamental, tax and identified diligence risks require separate treatment, with direct Seller recourse beyond the escrow and appropriate fraud protections. We also require express protection against pre-Closing leakage.

Please confirm Seller’s willingness to engage on price and these principal protections, and propose a data-room delivery schedule. All positions remain nonbinding and subject to definitive agreement.
